note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English; the original book gives Calotermes (Cryptotermes) gearyi sp. nov., type locality Dalby (Qld), described from several series taken in living trees and dead branches (hosts including Eucalyptus melliodora, E. rostrata, Callitris glauca). The original has only the alate and soldier sections and no worker description. In the Affinities sentence the OCR is defective: 'The soldier from C. primus in its larger size…', with the verb missing, read from the context as 'compared with C. primus…'; here C. primus is the C. primus of the genus Cryptotermes in the same book, a different taxon bearing the same specific name, not the Mirotermes (Paracapritermes) primus of the checklist, which the lead should note. OCR misreadings: 'postclypeuS' = postclypeus, 'shagreened' is the original term, 'molllocLora'/'melllodora'/'melliodora' all refer to Eucalyptus melliodora, 'fumlgatus' = fumigatus, 'takai' = taken, '1,43' uses a comma as decimal point, '6.60 - 6.75-' has a trailing dash that is OCR noise.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate: head small, the sides nearly parallel, compound eyes small (diameter 0.33), ocelli very small and touching the compound eyes, antennae 15- or 16-segmented (usually 16), pronotum wider than the head, wider than long, wings densely covered with scale-like spinules (especially on the veins). For the comparison with C. queenslandis see that species; the soldier, compared with C. primus, is larger, with antennal segment 3 longer and coloured, the frontal processes larger, the frons deeply concave, and compared with C. nocens it is larger, with antennal segment 3 and the frontal processes more developed.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dorsum and wing veins dark brown, venter and wing membrane slightly paler, legs and labrum yellow-brown. Head small, the sides nearly parallel, finely shagreened, with sparse short hairs. Compound eyes small (diameter 0.33) and protruding. Ocelli very small, touching the compound eyes. Behind the transverse suture there is on each side of the head a distinct frontal spot, in line with the ocelli and the lateral margins of the postclypeus. Antennae 15- or 16-segmented, usually 16; segment 3 often longer and wider than segment 2, sometimes segments 2, 3 and 4 equal in length; from segment 4 to segment 14 or 15 progressively longer and wider, the terminal segment shorter and narrower than the penultimate. Pronotum wider than the head, wider than long, strongly arched, the anterior margin with a wide shallow concavity, the sides slightly rounded, the posterior margin broadly rounded and slightly concave in the middle, the margins depressed and with short hairs of moderate length, the rest sparsely hairy. Wings of moderate length and narrow, densely covered with scale-like spinules, especially on the veins. Measurements: body length with wings 9.00—9.25 mm; body length without wings 5.50—7.00 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.43 mm; head length (to clypeal suture) 1.06 mm; head width 1.13 mm; pronotum length 0.69 mm; pronotum width 1.21 mm; forewing length 6.60—6.75 mm; forewing width 1.72 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Mandibles, postclypeus and frons black; vertex and lateral cervical sclerites dark reddish brown, the occipital region paler. Head slightly longer than wide, slightly narrower behind the compound eyes than at the middle, the posterior part broadly rounded, finely shagreened. Mandibles relatively long, with well-developed teeth. Frontal processes well developed, in side view distinctly raised and overhanging the frons, deeply cleft in the middle, extending laterally to the compound eyes; this extended area is concave and distinctly wrinkled in the middle. Near each end of the postclypeus there is a short stout horn-like projection, and a prolongation of the ventral part of the genae forms a similar projection. Compound eyes elongate-oval. Antennae 11—14-segmented, usually 12; segment 3 darkly coloured, usually as long as or longer than segment 2. Pronotum as wide as the head, the anterior margin upturned, deeply and widely concave in the middle, distinctly saw-toothed, the sides sharply to broadly rounded to the middle, the posterolateral angles broadly rounded, the posterior margin straight, the sides and posterior margin depressed, with sparse rather long hairs. Measurements: body length (head at 45° to the body) 6.50—7.00 mm; head length (from base to apex of mandibles) 2.16 mm; head length (from base to frontal processes) 1.28 mm; head length (from base to clypeal suture) 1.54 mm; head width 1.43 mm; pronotum length 0.84 mm; pronotum width 1.43 mm.
